observations: What I read: AGENTS.md (supplied as project instructions), all of docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md and docs/PROMPTS.md, the whole prepared request (decisions, dialoguePolicy, dialogueInstructions and all 23 panels in base.script), all of works/auto-6294ee8a2094/source/original.txt, all of works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/source-coverage.json, and the previous response script-all-r7.json for context. Every file was readable. To understand the added faces I opened these accepted panels with Read: 01-3, 03-1, 03-2, 03-3, 04-2, 04-3, 05-3 and 05-4. This does not certify any artwork. The request's script contains production.hands but no speakers/faces blocks, so I could not check the face registrations themselves, only the hands entries and the images. Reading order: I read the request's lettering fields in panel order before the source, then compared them with it.

No text changed. Every dialogue and caption string matches the source word for word, and each panel's textColumns join back into exactly its text string. This includes the re-wrapped 02-4, 04-1, 04-4, 06-1, 06-2 and 06-4. 05-4 is now a single column, which is still identical. The only split is still 01-2, where one Meera line becomes two balloons by the same speaker with nobody speaking in between. No turns are merged across another speaker.

Reading the lettering alone, it still holds together. 'the rest' (01-3) points back to Meera's list (01-2). 'here' (02-2) refers to the laptop in 02-1. 'And our team' (02-3) follows straight on from Ananya. Each question is answered in the next panel: 03-1 to 03-2, 03-2 to 03-3, 04-1 to 04-2 and 05-2 to 05-3. 'your concerns' (04-4) refers back to 04-2. The voices fit: Ananya calm, Meera polite, Ravi casual. Product roles (Practice on the laptop, Care on the staff phone, Health on Ravi's phone) and the vision separation (only 06-2 and 06-3 carry the WELBUK VISION label and vignette, and 06-1 keeps 'may') are unchanged. I found no medical claim, real data or invented feature.

The added characters fit the story. 01-3: Meera in the background still holds the receiver in her left hand and writes with her right, which matches 01-2 and strengthens Ananya's motive. 03-1: Meera typing at the desk gives Ravi someone to greet. 04-2 and 04-3: the backs of Ananya's and Ravi's heads keep Ananya left / Ravi right. 05-3: Ravi's back of head keeps Meera left / Ravi right. 05-4: Ananya and Meera waving from the doorway is a natural send-off after the reception walkthrough. In the image their raised hands match the new entries (Ananya's right, Meera's left), and Ravi waves with his right hand while holding the phone in his left.

The new hands entries contradict the phone records. In 03-2 Ravi's right hand is now 'holding his phone low at the desk (foreground)', and the image shows it. The accepted 03-3 image then shows a blue phone lying on the desk in front of him. But 03-2 and 03-3 have no ravi-phone prop entry, and 05-1 still says the phone was 'in Ravi's pocket' and that he 'took out his own phone'. In 05-3 the new hands entry says Ravi's left hand holds his phone in the foreground, and the image shows it in frame, but the prop still reads 'held by Ravi off-panel right' with heldBy 'none'.
The 'departure' section (used by 05-4) lists a costume for Ravi only. Ananya and Meera are now registered as visible in that panel, but the section has no costume entries for them.

Not blocking, for the artwork, storyboard and lettering reviews: (a) The 01-3 and 03-1 scene text still describes the desk as off-panel, or leaves Meera out, although she is now visible. (b) In 01-3 the stage should confirm that Ananya's gaze actually reads as directed at the desk. (c) In 03-2 Ravi is seen from behind on the left, facing right, so the near hand holding the phone may read as his left rather than the recorded right. (d) A blue phone also lies on the desk in 03-1 without an owner; it should be confirmed as Meera's or the clinic's, so it does not look like Ravi's phone before he arrives. None of these need new artwork; they are record and scene-text consistency points.

issues.problem: Ravi's phone record contradicts the new hands entries and the accepted art. 03-2 now has Ravi holding his phone at the desk, and 03-3 shows it lying on the desk. Yet 03-2 and 03-3 have no ravi-phone prop entry, and 05-1 still gives props.ravi-phone.before as 'in Ravi's pocket', with production.before saying he 'took out his own phone'. Add ravi-phone entries for 03-2 (heldBy ravi.right, or the hand that is actually visible) and 03-3 (on the desk, heldBy none). Then correct 05-1's before/after to a consistent history, such as put away after registration or carried since then.

In 05-3 the ravi-phone prop still says 'held by Ravi off-panel right' with heldBy 'none', but the new hands entry and the image show Ravi's left hand holding the phone in the foreground, in frame. Set during to the in-frame foreground hold and heldBy to ravi.left.

Ananya and Meera are now visible in 05-4, but the 'departure' section lists a costume for Ravi only. Add Ananya (teal kurta, open white coat, stethoscope worn but not in use) and Meera (blue kurta, white churidar, silver bangle) to departure.costumes, so costume continuity covers every visible character in this panel.

panels.observation: The source caption is kept word for word. It names Ananya and sets up the 'busy' premise that Meera's complaint in 01-2 depends on.
Meera's single source line is split at the ellipsis into two balloons by the same speaker, with nothing in between. The list gives 'everything' its referent.
Ananya's line is word for word, and 'the rest' depends on the 01-2 list. Meera, now visible in the background still mid-call, makes her motive clear on the page itself.
The onboarding caption is word for word, and evening light marks the time change. The Practice label names the source's 'laptop view of Welbuk Practice' and claims no feature.
The line is word for word. 'here' refers to the laptop in 02-1, and her considering team roles leads into Meera's line.
'And our team...' is word for word and continues 02-2 with no other speaker between them. The Care label matches the source's 'staff phone displaying Welbuk Care'.
'One team. Better coordination.' is word for word and only re-wrapped. It sums up 02-2 and 02-3, and Meera's silent nod is a manga reaction, not a dropped line.
Ravi's greeting and request are word for word. The newly visible Meera at the desk is who he greets, and 'Of course' in 03-2 answers his request.
The line is word for word. It answers 03-1 and asks the consent question that 03-3 replies to. Ravi's new foreground phone has no prop record (see issues).
'Yes, please.' answers the 03-2 consent question. The monitor shows blank fields only, matching 'no actual identifying data'.
'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' is word for word. His name follows from the registration, and the gesture to the chairs leads into page 4.
The greeting is word for word and only re-wrapped. 'Tell me what brings you in' is the question 04-2 answers, and the same costumes show it is the same visit.
'I've been feeling tired lately.' answers 04-1 word for word as a routine concern with no diagnosis. Ananya's back of head on the left keeps the 04-1 sides.
The caption is word for word, backed by a silent attentive listener and the closed laptop. Ravi's back of head on the right keeps the sides.
The line is word for word and only re-wrapped. 'your concerns' refers back to 04-2, with no instruments in use and no treatment advice.
Meera's line is word for word and keeps the careful 'designed to help'. The prop history still says the phone came from his pocket, which contradicts 03-2 and 03-3 (see issues).
Ravi's question is word for word and depends on Meera's explanation in 05-1. The abstract cards stand in for the source's 'appointments and health information' without showing any data.
'That's the idea' answers 05-2, and 'what is available to you' is kept word for word. The prop record conflicts with the in-frame phone hold (see issues).
The caption is word for word. Ananya and Meera waving from the doorway makes a logical send-off for 'leaves, reassured', but their costumes are missing from the departure section (see issues).
The caption is word for word and only re-wrapped, keeping the conditional 'may'. The non-vision train panel carries the change of time and place.
The 'WELBUK VISION' label the source asks for and the caption are word for word inside the vignette. The re-wrap changes no words, and nothing suggests a launched referral feature.
The caption is word for word. The repeated vision label and the vignette keep the family wellness app conceptual.
The three product labels and the final caption are word for word and only re-wrapped. The present-day group ties Practice, Care and Health back to 02-1, 02-3 and 05-2.
